title: bug: Stopping the container with SIGTERM fails
body:
### Describe the bug

Upon sending a SIGTERM signal (eg. with `podman stop`), not all processes in the container stop properly, and the container has to be killed eventually.  

Example output trying to stop a running instance directly:
```
$ podman stop homarr
WARN[0010] StopSignal SIGTERM failed to stop container homarr in 10 seconds, resorting to SIGKILL
```

**TL;DR:** the `logger` instance in `wssServer.cjs` also logs to Redis, and that Redis connection is still in the event loop, so the process never exits. Detailed rundown below.

---

The problem seems to be that the `node apps/websocket/wssServer.cjs` process never stops, even though a SIGTERM is sent by `run.sh`
https://github.com/homarr-labs/homarr/blob/d218170ec28a70b80c521efd1482164087d46e05/scripts/run.sh#L50

SIGTERM is properly handled in the websocket "app"
https://github.com/homarr-labs/homarr/blob/d218170ec28a70b80c521efd1482164087d46e05/apps/websocket/src/main.ts#L60

...however several handles are still open after the `wss` instance is closed (`wtfnode` output for readability):
```
[WTF Node?] open handles:
- File descriptors: (note: stdio always exists)
  - fd 2 (tty) (stdio)
  - fd 1 (tty) (stdio)
- Sockets:
  - 127.0.0.1:60676 -> 127.0.0.1:6379
  - 127.0.0.1:60690 -> 127.0.0.1:6379
  - 127.0.0.1:60700 -> 127.0.0.1:6379
  - 127.0.0.1:60702 -> 127.0.0.1:6379
  - 127.0.0.1:60712 -> 127.0.0.1:6379
  - 127.0.0.1:60718 -> 127.0.0.1:6379
- Servers:
  - <unknown address>
    - Listeners:
      - request: WebSocketServer2 @ /app/apps/websocket/wssServer.cjs:4951
```
The port seems to be the default Redis port.

It seems that it imports a logger from `@homarr/log` and adds a [Redis Transport](https://github.com/homarr-labs/homarr/blob/dev/packages/log/src/redis-transport.ts) to log to
https://github.com/homarr-labs/homarr/blob/d218170ec28a70b80c521efd1482164087d46e05/packages/log/src/index.ts#L28

To cross-check, I have set the `DISABLE_REDIS_LOGS` envvar for the container based on the following branch in the logger
https://github.com/homarr-labs/homarr/blob/d218170ec28a70b80c521efd1482164087d46e05/packages/log/src/index.ts#L26
...and stopping with SIGTERM behaves properly afterwards.

This, unfortunately, breaks other parts though, like `analytics`
```log
2025-07-22T21:21:36.052Z info: Starting schedule of cron job analytics.
2025-07-22T21:21:36.053Z error: Failed to run job 'analytics': TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'get')
/app/apps/tasks/tasks.cjs:644759
      const data = await lastDataClient.get(lastChannelName);
                                        ^

TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'get')
    at Object.getLastDataAsync (/app/apps/tasks/tasks.cjs:644759:41)
    at Object.onCallbackErrorAsync [as onCallbackError] (/app/apps/tasks/tasks.cjs:644989:35)
    at catchingCallbackAsync (/app/apps/tasks/tasks.cjs:645031:47)
    at process.processTicksAndRejections (node:internal/process/task_queues:105:5)
    at async Object.onStartAsync (/app/apps/tasks/tasks.cjs:645062:9)
    at async Object.startAllAsync (/app/apps/tasks/tasks.cjs:645134:11)
    at async /app/apps/tasks/tasks.cjs:679419:3
```


### Steps to reproduce

- start the container according to the docs
- run `podman stop` or `docker stop`

After the built-in timeout, observe a SIGKILL be sent.

### Impact

- potentially long wait times on container stop events
- the auto update feature of Podman rolls back the previous version due to incorrect shutdown of the existing container
- "failed" exit state (eg. when running with systemd, as quadlet)

### Additional information

Tested with
- manual `podman run`
- with systemd quadlets
- on the dev branch
- on v1.28.1

I guess either the process has to be exited "directly" [after closing the websocket server](https://github.com/homarr-labs/homarr/blob/d218170ec28a70b80c521efd1482164087d46e05/apps/websocket/src/main.ts#L63), or the Redis connection would somehow need to be closed gracefully at the same stage.

Thank you in advance for looking into this, and for your development efforts on this great project!

### Version

1.28.1

### Installation method

Other (describe in "additional information")

### Browser

Firefox

full_comments.body: Hi, can you verify that this issue still exists in 1.30.0?

Hi, I had tested with the dev branch previously, but just confirmed the same behavior with v1.30.0 from the registry:
```
$ podman run  \
  --rm --name homarr \
  -p 7575:7575 \
  -e SECRET_ENCRYPTION_KEY='1ce680cf744e7b0da0d8a175b3207ecd382578cd2cce611f31f6f4a701fda645' \
  -d ghcr.io/homarr-labs/homarr:v1.30.0
5c8a70707f45cf3ce67f76fbe5959d63a9fd4730c5d3bf13124966406e8245be

$ podman stop homarr
WARN[0010] StopSignal SIGTERM failed to stop container homarr in 10 seconds, resorting to SIGKILL 
homarr
```

Inspecting container logs with `podman logs -f homarr` seem to indicate the same behavior (receiving SIGTERM, logging it, then continuing to run):
```
Received SIGTERM. Shutting down...
2025-07-23T08:35:32.489Z info: SIGTERM
2025-07-23T08:35:32.575Z info: ➖ Connection (0) 1006
```

**Edit:** Additionally, it seems that even after setting the `DISABLE_REDIS_LOGS` envvar, the container will fail to stop. It seems that bash `wait` without any arguments will wait for _all_ background tasks to finish. I had forgot to mention previously that locally I changed
https://github.com/homarr-labs/homarr/blob/d218170ec28a70b80c521efd1482164087d46e05/scripts/run.sh#L51
to
```bash
wait $NGINX_PID $TASKS_PID $WSS_PID $NEXTJS_PID
```
since at that point the Redis background task is not called to be terminated yet.

I see the same something similar in docker:

Milliseconds after running `docker compose stop homarr` I get:
```
21:M 04 Aug 2025 06:10:16.159 * Background saving terminated with success
Received SIGTERM. Shutting down...
2025-08-04T06:10:41.056Z info: SIGTERM
2025-08-04T06:10:41.074Z info: ➖ Connection (2) 1006
2025-08-04T06:10:41.099Z info: ➖ Connection (1) 1006
2025-08-04T06:10:41.104Z info: ➖ Connection (0) 1006
```
But after that it hangs for about 10 seconds (the default timeout) until docker's stop function times out and docker sends a SIGKILL to take down the container.
